Closing verdict. Merged as 73e90b296e2 (Gerrit 3173, LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1). gerrit/main tip equals the pushed SHA, so the landed tree is byte-identical to the verified tree -- no server-side rebase.

All four ACs re-run against the landed tree:

- AC1 PASS. gen_env_registry.py --check exit 0; tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py 25 passed, including the new test_every_canonical_env_name_is_documented, which derives _SECTIONS x _canonical_env_name and the documented rows independently and asserts no literal count.
- AC2 PASS. git grep -n 'REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE|github-api' -- scripts .github tests returns nothing (exit 1). Pre-state was the 14 hits across 5 files the AC predicted. tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py 35 passed.
- AC3 PASS, checked by section membership rather than line number. [0.13.0] carries neither the force_close nor the openai-chat bullet; [0.14.0] carries both plus the REBAR_HLC entry; [Unreleased] ### Changed carries exactly 4 bullets.
- AC4 PASS. scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check exit 0 (active=648, new=28 all admitted, increased=0). make verify green: 20117 passed, 27 skipped, 41m07s, exit 0.

Three scope deviations, each argued in the commit message: the bootstrap keyword was removed rather than made required (its only caller is now the bootstrap path, so a required-but-unread keyword is dead weight); CHANGELOG and release-note entries were added for the canary retirement, which the plan did not enumerate but which is breaking for any repo running a copy of the workflow; and the detect_config.py plus docs/architecture.md edits were dropped because the plan's premise for them was false -- detect_env_vars consumes registry.scan() and its own _derived_env_names, never render(), so a render()-only change adds zero census entries. The plan was corrected before review, and the correction shrank scope.

No force override was used.
